canonical_definition: In-Context Learning (ICL) is the capability of pre-trained large language models (LLMs) to perform new tasks by leveraging input–output demonstrations or exemplars provided within the prompt context during inference, without parameter updates or fine-tuning. This ability relies on prepending task-related examples to the query, enabling the model to acquire task-relevant skills within the context window through mechanisms such as attention to demonstration content. While often operationalized as few-shot learning (requiring limited examples), some definitions extend it to zero-shot scenarios, emphasizing its parameter-free nature and emergence with increased training task diversity. Disagreements exist in scope, with some authors focusing on strict demonstration-guided adaptation versus broader context-driven skill acquisition.
